item.title: Turkish drillship arrives in Somali waters for historic first offshore oil drilling
item.description: Somalia is preparing to launch its first-ever offshore oil drilling operation, with a Turkish state-owned drillship expected to arrive in Somali waters later this week. The Çağrı Bey, operated by the Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO), is scheduled to reach Somalia around April 10, marking a milestone in a partnership that could reshape the economic prospects of one of the world's poorest nations.

item.title: Wall Street firm sends analyst into Strait of Hormuz by speedboat
item.description:
Citrini Research, the small Wall Street firm that rattled markets earlier this year with a bearish call on artificial intelligence, has turned its unconventional methods toward the ongoing crisis in the Strait of Hormuz — dispatching a field analyst into one of the world's most dangerous waterways by speedboat to gather firsthand intelligence on Iranian shipping controls.

The firm said it sent an employee referred to as "Analyst #3" to Oman's Musandam Peninsula, where he boarded a GPS-less speedboat and pushed toward the center of the strait armed with $15,000 in cash and concealed recording equipment, according to The Wall Street Journal. The analyst traveled within view of the Iranian coastline, observing drones overhead and Iranian patrol boats operating nearby, before being intercepted and briefly detained. His phone was confiscated, and his observations were later reconstructed during an eight-hour debrief after he returned safely.

item.title: Trump warns 'whole civilization will die tonight' as Iran deadline nears
item.description:
President Trump escalated his rhetoric against Iran on Tuesday, warning that "a whole civilization will die tonight, never to be brought back again" if Tehran does not agree to reopen the Strait of Hormuz by his 8 p.m. Eastern deadline. The ultimatum comes on the 38th day of the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, which began on February 28 with what the White House called "Operation Epic Fury".

Airstrikes hit two bridges and a train station inside Iran on Tuesday morning, while Iranian officials called on young people to form human chains around power plants Trump has threatened to destroy. Iran's president, Masoud Pezeshkian, posted on X that 14 million Iranians had volunteered to fight and said he would join them.

item.title: Eni announces 2 Tcf gas discovery off Egypt's coast
item.description: Eni announced on Tuesday a gas and condensate discovery offshore Egypt estimated at about 2 trillion cubic feet of gas in place, the latest in a string of Mediterranean finds by the Italian energy company that includes a separate 1 trillion cubic feet discovery off Libya's coast last month.

item.title: US strikes Kharg Island again as war with Iran intensifies
item.description: US forces struck military targets on Iran's strategic Kharg Island on Tuesday as the six-week-old war entered one of its most volatile phases, with airstrikes pounding Tehran, Iranian missiles hitting Saudi Arabia and Israel, and President Donald Trump warning that "a whole civilization will die tonight" if Iran does not agree to a deal by his 8 p.m. Eastern deadline.

item.title: IOM says nearly 1,000 migrants died in Mediterranean in 2026 so far
item.description: More than 80 migrants are missing after a boat capsized in the central Mediterranean Sea over the weekend, the United Nations migration agency said Tuesday, in what is part of a devastating stretch of shipwrecks that has made 2026 one of the deadliest years for Mediterranean crossings in over a decade.

item.title: China and Russia veto UN Strait of Hormuz resolution hours before Trump deadline
item.description:
The United Nations Security Council on Tuesday failed to adopt a resolution aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz after China and Russia vetoed the Bahrain-drafted measure, leaving the international community without a diplomatic framework to address Iran's blockade of the waterway just hours before President Donald Trump's self-imposed deadline for Iran to reopen the strait or face strikes on its civilian infrastructure.

The resolution, which had been repeatedly diluted over two weeks of negotiations to avoid precisely such an outcome, received broad support from a majority of the 15-member council but could not overcome the vetoes of two permanent members. The vote was held at 11 a.m. Eastern, nine hours before Trump's 8 p.m. deadline, which he set for Iran to agree to a deal or face attacks on its power plants and bridges.

item.title: Vance says he's 'here to help' Orban win Hungary election
item.description: Vice President JD Vance arrived in Budapest on Tuesday and openly endorsed Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's reelection bid, while accusing the European Union and Ukrainian intelligence services of meddling in Hungary's April 12 parliamentary elections — claims he made without providing evidence.

item.title: UK bars Ye from entering country, Wireless Festival canceled
item.description:
The British government on Tuesday denied Ye, the rapper formerly known as Kanye West, permission to enter the United Kingdom, prompting the immediate cancellation of this year's Wireless Festival in London. The Home Office rejected Ye's application for an Electronic Travel Authorisation on the grounds that his presence would not be "conducive to the public good," according to the BBC.

Ye had been announced as the sole headliner for the three-day Wireless Festival, scheduled for July 10-12 in Finsbury Park, where he was expected to perform before roughly 150,000 attendees. Festival Republic, the event's organizer, confirmed the cancellation and said refunds would be issued to all ticket holders.

item.title: Iran severs all diplomatic channels with US ahead of Trump's Hormuz deadline
item.description:
Iran on Tuesday shut down all diplomatic and indirect communication channels with the United States, according to the state-run Tehran Times, in a dramatic escalation that came just hours before President Donald Trump's self-imposed deadline for Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The move effectively closes off avenues for last-minute negotiations as the six-week-old war enters one of its most dangerous phases.

"Iran has closed all diplomatic and indirect channels of communication with the United States. Any and all message exchanges have also been suspended," the Tehran Times reported. The Wall Street Journal, citing a Middle Eastern official, reported that the cutoff of direct diplomacy was intended to signal Tehran's disapproval of Trump's threats, though it noted that some mediated discussions may still be ongoing.

item.title: EV sales hit records in Australia, Europe as fuel crisis reshapes auto market
item.description: Soaring gasoline prices driven by the ongoing conflict in Iran are reshaping the global auto market, pushing electric vehicle sales to record highs in several countries and sparking a wave of consumer interest in battery-powered alternatives — even as the picture in the United States remains more complicated.

item.title: Tehran's Rafi-Nia Synagogue destroyed in US-Israeli strikes
item.description: Joint US-Israeli airstrikes early Tuesday "completely destroyed" the Rafi-Nia Synagogue in central Tehran, according to reports from Iran's Shargh newspaper and semi-official Mehr news agency, adding a charged dimension to the ongoing military campaign against Iran that began on February 28.

item.title: Leaked transcript shows Orbán offered to serve Putin
item.description:
Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán told Russian President Vladimir Putin he was ready to assist him "in any way" during a phone call last October, according to a Hungarian government transcript reviewed by Bloomberg and published on Monday.

"Yesterday our friendship rose to such a high level that I can help in any way," Orbán told Putin during the October 17, 2025, conversation, according to the transcript. "In any matter where I can be of assistance, I am at your service."

To illustrate his readiness to serve, Orbán referenced a well-known Hungarian children's tale in which a mouse rescues a lion from a trap after the lion had previously spared the mouse's life.

item.title: UK, Canada push back on Trump's Iran threats as 8 p.m. deadline nears
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Tuesday urged all parties in the Iran conflict to respect international law, hours before President Donald Trump's self-imposed deadline to launch attacks on Iranian bridges and power plants. In Britain, the government reinforced that it had authorized U.S. use of British military bases only for defensive operations, not strikes on civilian infrastructure.

item.title: Kuwait orders residents indoors as Trump's Iran deadline looms
item.description: Kuwait's Ministry of Interior on Tuesday urged all citizens and residents to stay home and avoid going outdoors from midnight to 6:00 a.m. on Wednesday, April 8, citing precautionary security measures as regional tensions reach a critical juncture. The directive, described as a "precautionary measure," comes as President Donald Trump's 8 p.m. Eastern deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approaches Tuesday evening, with the president warning of devastating strikes on Iranian infrastructure if no deal is reached.

item.title: White House denies nuclear strike plans as Iran deadline looms
item.description: The White House on Tuesday forcefully denied that Vice President JD Vance had suggested the United States might use nuclear weapons against Iran, after his remarks about unused military options fueled widespread speculation amid escalating tensions over President Donald Trump's latest deadline for Tehran.

item.title: Pakistan's Sharif urges Trump to extend Iran deadline two weeks
item.description:
Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday called on President Donald Trump to extend his deadline for Iran by two weeks, issuing a public plea just hours before Trump's 8 p.m. Eastern time ultimatum that has threatened devastating strikes on Iranian power plants and bridges.

"I earnestly request President Trump to extend the deadline for two weeks," Sharif wrote in a message posted on X, according to The Wall Street Journal. He also called on Tehran to temporarily reopen the Strait of Hormuz for the same two-week period "as a sign of goodwill," and urged all warring parties to observe a ceasefire across all fronts to allow diplomacy to produce a lasting resolution.

item.title: Trump sets 8 p.m. deadline for Iran to reopen Hormuz
item.description:
More than five weeks after the United States and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury against Iran on February 28, the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to most commercial shipping, triggering what the International Energy Agency has called the "largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market." On Tuesday, President Donald Trump set an 8 p.m. ET deadline for Iran to reopen the strait or face the destruction of its power plants and civilian infrastructure, posting on social media that "a whole civilization will die tonight."

The narrow waterway between Iran and Oman normally carries roughly 20% of global oil trade and a similar share of liquefied natural gas shipments. Since the conflict began, daily vessel crossings have plummeted by more than 90%, from an average of 138 ships per day to single digits, according to Goldman Sachs, which warned that countries could soon face outright oil shortages. Iran has maintained a selective passage regime, exporting its own oil while permitting transit only to nations that "pay a toll" and denying access to all others.

item.title: IDF warns of rising Iranian missile fire as Trump's deadline nears
item.description:
The Israel Defense Forces warned late Tuesday that missile fire toward Israeli territory could intensify "in the coming hours" as President Donald Trump's 8 p.m. Eastern deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approached with no deal in sight.

In a statement, the IDF urged the public to "remain vigilant, alert, and act responsibly, while continuing to follow the Home Front Command's instructions". The warning came as Iran fired fresh salvos of ballistic missiles at central and southern Israel on Tuesday, with cluster munitions striking multiple locations in the Sharon plain, according to the IDF. Earlier in the day, the military had urged Iranians to avoid train travel nationwide, before confirming strikes on a railway bridge in Kashan that killed at least two people.

item.title: Iranians form human chains at power plants as energy strikes loom
item.description: As President Donald Trump's 8 p.m. ET deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approached on Tuesday, Iranian authorities launched a nationwide campaign calling on young people to form "human chains" around power plants and other critical infrastructure in a bid to deter threatened American strikes.
